title: Are You a Godless Christian?
summary: We plan as if we rule our own lives, but we are a mist. Live every day saying, "If the Lord wills."
exhortation: This passage has always poked my heart and convicted me. I come back to it often and ask myself: am I a godless Christian? Do I go about my daily life without any awareness of the supremacy and sovereignty of God over my life? Do I functionally operate as if I'm the ruler of the universe: "I will do this, I will do that," with no thought of what the Lord would have me do?

A pragmatism can creep into my life that kills the spiritual life. I would never say I'm the lord of my own universe, but I can think it subtly: I plan everything, I order my day. "Yet you do not know what tomorrow will bring." We act like we do. I do. I plan for tomorrow as if everything will go on just as it did before. But we don't know how long our lives will be or how things will turn out. We are not the rulers of the universe.

So what should we do instead? Acknowledge that we are a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes. That could make us feel small and weak, but it's meant to reveal a deep truth: we serve a greater and more awesome God. We are not the kings and queens of the universe. The Lord alone sits on his throne, and he alone knows the number of our days.

So instead we say, "If the Lord wills." We live at the Lord's pleasure, and it is a richer, more satisfying way to live. It is how God designed us: to look at tomorrow and say, "I can't guarantee it," and to live every moment in submission to his will. "Lord, what would you have me do today?" This is why staying in God's word is the most important thing a Christian can do. He has revealed his plan and told us what to do with our lives. So if you've been drifting, inch by inch, into a life that isn't dependent on the Lord, let's go before him this morning and ask him to reveal any pride that lives as if he doesn't exist, and humbly submit ourselves to him for his glory and his kingdom.
prayer: Lord, thank you for your faithfulness. You have promised in your word to keep this world going and bring the seasons in their time. When we say in our pride that we know what tomorrow will bring, we take glory away from your faithfulness and your grace toward us. Remind us that it's because of your faithfulness and grace that we know the sun will come up tomorrow.

For those of us who feel convicted that we've been going in our own strength and power, help us throw our lives on your grace and faithfulness. Help us take up your glory, die to our own, and experience the joy of walking in your ways. In Jesus' name, amen.
